subjectUnderTest: src/reference/claim-reference.ts (ReferenceClaimStore) — the small reference/test-double model, NOT production code
rootCause: ReferenceClaimStore.claim() checked `row.owner !== null` (an active-owner guard) BEFORE checking whether the incoming fingerprint matched the bound fingerprint. So a same-id/different-fingerprint request arriving while the invocation ALREADY has an active owner reports outcome "in-progress" instead of "conflict" — a label/branch ordering difference from the literal TLA+ ClaimOwner guard order, and from this harness's own naive test expectation of a single canonical outcome label.
severityAssessment: NOT a safety violation. Both "in-progress" and "conflict" outcomes refuse the request: neither claims ownership under the mismatched fingerprint, and neither is a state a fingerprint-mismatched caller can reach a dispatch from. The actual invariant under test (SameIdDifferentFingerprintNeverExecutes: a same-id/different-fingerprint request never claims and never dispatches) held throughout — only the specific outcome-label assertion in the test itself was too strict / wrong about which label to expect in this branch.
fix: Rewrote the test to assert the actual safety invariant directly (second claim() call is never "claimed", the original owner/fingerprint binding is unchanged, and a dispatch attempt by the rejected actor never succeeds) instead of asserting one specific outcome label. Left ReferenceClaimStore's guard ordering as-is since it does not affect any checked invariant — documented the ordering explicitly in a comment on the regression test so a future reader does not reintroduce the same over-strict assertion.
regressionTest: src/tests/reference-model.property.test.ts > 'reference model: claim/dispatch invariants' > 'SameIdDifferentFingerprintNeverExecutes: a fingerprint mismatch never claims ownership nor gets dispatched' — runs permanently as part of the suite (fast-check numRuns default, minimized shrink retained via fixed property generators).
